name: Which custom cabinet features actually improve kitchen storage?

mainEntity.name: Which custom cabinet features actually improve kitchen storage?

acceptedAnswer.text:
The most useful storage features depend on what you store and where you work, not on how many accessories a showroom displays. Deep drawers often help with pots and dishes, while narrow pull-outs, tray dividers, trash storage, and appliance garages solve more specific problems.

Context: Adding every accessory can consume cabinet volume and increase cost. Elite Remodeling & Design can adapt storage to the kitchen’s intended use during layout and design development.

Key factors:
- Heavy cookware and drawer weight capacity
- Pantry and food-storage needs
- Recycling, trash, and cleaning supplies
- Small appliances and countertop workspace

Practical guidance: Inventory your current cabinets and note what is hard to reach or repeatedly left on counters. Mark the desired location of each major storage category on the plan.

Prioritizing high-use storage usually produces more value than adding features everywhere.
acceptedAnswer.description: Prioritize storage around your real habits: deep drawers for cookware, pull-outs for narrow spaces, tray dividers, organized waste storage, and pantry capacity. Inventory what is difficult to store before selecting accessories.
